_doc: One entry per shipped model. Code finds models here (src/models.js), never by hard-coded tables. Convention: after 'rot' (Euler degrees, applied in 'order', default XYZ) the model faces +z (bow/head), up +y. 'fit' says where y = 0 goes: 'center' (animals: box centre at the origin, scaled so the length along z matches), 'bottom' (boats: lowest point at y = 0, then lowered by draft_m), 'base' (trees: base at y = 0, scaled by height). 'tint' is a per-species colour multiplier. A model with one file has 'file'; a model with detail tiers has 'files': { tier: { file, tris, bytes } } (tiers listed in 'tiers.order', best first; src/lod.js picks by distance and bakes the far impostor at run time). Files live in models/ as <file>.glb.txt (base64, what the published page fetches). 'bytes' is the size of that .glb.txt. Only slimmed files ship (textures <= 2k, webp). Tree tiers are made by tools/assets/node/treelod.mjs from the full model. Assets owns this file. Single-file models under ~1k triangles carry no tiers: LOD.tiersFor draws the mesh near and the baked impostor far. 'shadow': { tier, far_m } makes one tier (low) cast the shadow for every tier, in one draw, out to far_m from the camera (src/lod.js, LOD.shadowSource; trees, 31 Oct).

models.name: Friendship V

nodes.nozzle: <jet>_nozzle: steering, rotate about local y; +rad turns the outlet to STARBOARD, so Boats nozCmd (+ = jet to port, x 30 deg) is rotation.y = -nozCmd * 0.524
nodes.bucket: <jet>_bucket: reversing bucket, rotate about local x; shipped raised at rotation.x = +1.05 rad (ahead), 0 = fully down (astern)
nodes.bridge: hd only, under hull/bridge: screen_chart, screen_radar, screen_engines, screen_aux, screen_engines3, screen_engines4 (the 2x2 engine monitors), screen_camera, screen_heading(2), screen_navdata(2) (atlas UVs, fv_screens); lever_thr_0..3 and lever_bkt_0..3 (rotate about local x; 0 port outer .. 3 stbd outer), helm_tiller (local y), helm_joystick; helm_eye (empty at the helmsman's eyes)
nodes.decks: (GA, photo-corrected 30 Oct night) main deck y 2.3; bulwark cap 3.25; risers 2.6, 2.9; second level floor 4.63, lounge from z -3.1 forward, windowed open-backed sides to -9.0, open aft to -12.2; top deck 7.75 (raised 0.7 to Matt's side photo; z -11.5..2.0); arch beam 9.35; masthead light 11.14; port stair bay z -4.8..-2.05
nodes.jets_z: the jets hang off the transoms at z -14.0 (GA: the hulls end there; sloped boarding platforms run aft over the jets to -17.05)
nodes.mooring: under 'mooring': cleat_<bow|bow_quarter|quarter|stern>_<port|stbd> (at the horns' height) and chock_<same>_<port|stbd> (in the bulwark plate), at Boats' positions of 31 Oct

models.particulars: 34.1 m LOA (98.8 ft registered) x 9.45 m, 1.40 m load draft (USCG 1040508, per Boats); IMO 8994099; Gladding-Hearn hull 303, delivered June 1996, Incat design; four 1,205 hp MTU diesels, four waterjets (make and model not found: docs/vessel-models.md)
models.author: tools/assets/vessels/build.py (procedural, from published particulars, deck plan and photographs)
sources: USCG documentation 1040508 via https://intelligence.marinelink.com/vessels/vessel/friendship-v-308326 (112 ft LOA, 31 ft beam, 4.6 ft draft, 35 ft height)
https://www.barharborwhales.com/our-boats/ (friendshipv-scaled-1.jpg: lines, layout, livery)
https://shipbuildinghistory.com/shipyards/small/gladdinghearn.htm (builder record)
models.tiers_doc: hd ~77k tris: lofted demihulls with the heavy rubber fendering; the main cabin and the second level (its sides leaning in), the windscreen across her front only (eight panes, broad black posts), the raked front face carrying the WHALE WATCHING / PUFFINS logo; the tubular arch with two open-array radars, the mast and its lights, the whips; five SOLAS liferaft canisters on the stern platform with straps and releases, boarding ladders; deck lamps and navigation lights (node 'lights': light_mast, light_steaming, light_side_port, light_side_stbd, light_stern, light_deck_*); the bridge fitted out inside; jets with nozzles and buckets as nodes. mid ~10k, low ~1.2k, then the impostor
models.physics_origin_doc: Boats' physics origin (transom on the waterline) in this model's fitted frame (frame_m is centred): draw the model at the body + 17.05 m along her keel
models.note: Lines, layout and paint traced off Matt's photographs (29 Oct 2026: broadside from the port quarter and a stern three-quarter), each matched by a fitted camera and overlaid (docs/vessel-models.md). Paint as she is now: all white, the whale-tail graphic on the bows; no lettering (her name, phone number, 'WHALE WATCH' left off). Jets generic.

frame_m.doc: the hull: transom to bow head, keel to whip tops. The jets and buckets stand 1.7 m proud aft and are left out, so every tier fits to the same frame and the hull sits on her 34.1 m

models.materials_doc: glossy white marine paint over aluminium; grey non-skid decks (Poly Haven concrete_pavement normals, textures/dock, CC0); stainless rails; tinted glass; powder-coated bench frames.
models.tex_doc: tex_mb: GPU memory of the tier's textures with mips (width x height x 4 x 4/3); materials: draw calls when lod.js draws the tier (MODELS.bake merges by material)
models.pbr_doc: materials carry real roughness (and, for the stainless, metalness) maps from scans (textures/vessels); MODELS keeps their metal, lit by the sky's environment map
models.livery_doc: Matt's photos, 30 Oct 2026 (starboard bow under way, stern, starboard at dusk): white, blue boot-top, blue bulwark aft with a blue half-moon below the rub rail, FRIENDSHIP V forward; blue band along the second level with the wave and 288-2386; the flag on the roof fascia; WHALE WATCHING / PUFFINS on her front; FRIENDSHIP V / WILMINGTON, DE across the stern. Each side has its own half of the livery so the lettering reads correctly on both
models.license_note: Model CC0, except the logo on her front (texture fv_logo, textures/vessels/bhwwc_logo.png): Bar Harbor Whale Watch Co.'s mark, supplied by Matt, shown only on their own vessel.

animate.doc: hd tier's moving parts (Matt, 31 Oct). sliders: the bridge's sliding side panes; translate the node along dir (model frame) from 0 (shut) to travel_m (open), on a click. wipers: rotate node about axis (model frame, through the node's origin, the pivot) by sweep_sign * a, a from 0 (parked) to sweep_rad and back (about 1.2 s a stroke), and rotate its blade child by the opposite angle about the same axis so the blade stays upright (a pantograph); off: ease back to 0. In mid and low they are parked geometry, not nodes.

models.colliders_doc: convex pieces (tools/assets/vessels/colliders.py), each <= 32 points, in the file's own frame (metres, bow +z, waterline y 0): scale with the model's fit. The hull in slices to her main deck, a catamaran's demihulls apart with the bridge deck over the tunnel on its own, the superstructure above

models.tiers_doc: hd ~46k tris (lofted hull with flare, raked stem and a sheer sweeping up into the forecastle bulwark; grey below, white above deck 3 aft and round the forecastle; hull windows and portholes; the anchors; the transom's marina recess and slot windows; balcony decks 4-6 at the deck plan's 3.34 m cabin pitch; the forward superstructure lofted as one raked sweep (deck 4 enclosed, the bridge on deck 5 glazed round its front, deck 6's glazed forward room under a roof sweeping down from the top deck), white deck-edge lines, deck 7's house and the sun deck with rounded noses; the aft terraces with rounded ends; lifeboats on davits; arched glass roof, funnel casing and stacks, radomes, the raked radar mast, crane, forecastle windlasses and bow crane; propellers and rudders as nodes), mid ~10k, low ~2.9k, then the impostor
models.physics_origin_doc: Boats' physics origin (transom on the waterline) in this model's fitted frame (frame_m is centred): draw the model at the body + 71.0 m along her keel

frame_m.doc: the hull, keel to the mast top; bridge wings and rudders stand outside it, so every tier fits to the same frame

models.materials_doc: painted steel (glossy white superstructure, grey hull); teak on the open decks, the balcony floors and the cap rails (Poly Haven wood_floor_deck's planks and seams in the colour of the wood_planks scan; textures/dock, CC0); white-painted rail posts and wires; glass balustrades; grey non-skid on the forecastle (concrete_pavement normals). The low tier draws the teak as flat colour.
models.impostor_doc: 8 views at 512 px (colour 512x4096 and normal 256x2048 atlases, ~12 MB of GPU memory with mips), lit by the sun through its normal atlas as the tree cards are; it takes over from the low tier at 2000 m (she is ~170 px long there on a 1080p screen, ~3 px per card pixel) and is drawn to 16 km

models.pbr_doc: materials carry real roughness (and, for the stainless, metalness) maps from scans (textures/vessels); MODELS keeps their metal, lit by the sky's environment map
models.colliders_doc: convex pieces (tools/assets/vessels/colliders.py), each <= 32 points, in the file's own frame (metres, bow +z, waterline y 0): scale with the model's fit. tiers._doc: Detail tiers a model may carry, best first. 'hd' ~25k tris (right by the boat), 'mid' ~6k, 'low' ~1.5k (card-culled foliage, grown to keep the crown's density). Past 'low' comes the impostor LOD.impostor bakes at run time, then nothing (the terrain's canopy texture). A model without a tier falls back to the next best it has.

textures._doc: Shared textures in textures/ (Assets). Layouts are in docs/facades.md. All of these are procedural stand-ins made by tools/assets/facades.py (CC0, this project) until photographs replace individual tiles; each tile is 2 m x 2 m of wall or roof and tiles seamlessly.

windows.alpha: 1 over frame and glass, 0 outside the frame
windows.glass_mask: blue >= 0.9 where glass is (mullions are dark lines that break it)
windows.author: procedural (facades.py)

rocks.note: colour as photographed, not grey-balanced; see textures/rocks/README.md. Same index order as levels/downeast/manifest.json rocks.
rocks.author: Poly Haven

moss_01.reads_as: hair-cap moss (Polytrichum-like) stems, 10 cut-out cards on one sheet: 8 short tufts, 2 long stems; alpha = cut-out
moss_01.use: not placed yet: for World's mossy forest floor and rock tops above the splash zone, as instanced crossed cards near the camera (<= 15 m), a texture on the ground beyond
moss_01.from: Matt's download (moss_01_4k, 19 Oct), 4k EXR normal converted raw, downsized to 1k

fill._doc: Mineral-fill swatch palette for the Critical Zone editor's fill brushes: textures/fill/palette.json (one entry per swatch: tiles, source, measured D50/sorting/roundedness/densities). Grouped by class. See textures/fill/README.md. Boulder/cobble classes also ship as individual de-lit clast stamps (textures/fill/clasts/) to be scattered, never tiled.

docks._doc: Docks are built by src/docks.js from a dock.json (docs/docks.md); styles in textures/dock/styles.json. Baked prefabs are listed as models with kind 'prefab'.

materials._doc: Terrain surface materials (Assets). One entry per material; textures/terrain/<id>/ holds colour.jpg (sRGB as photographed), normal.jpg (OpenGL tangent space), height.png (8-bit, stretched to the 0.5-99.5 % range of the source; height_range_src keeps that range in the source's 0..1 units) and rough.jpg, all 1024 px, seamless, made by tools/assets/terrainmats.py. tile_m = real-world width of one tile in metres (Poly Haven's measured dimensions). Packing for the terrain (no new samplers): array A (uRocks) layer = colour.rgb + height in alpha, array B (uRocksN) layer = normal.rgb + roughness in alpha, one layer per material, layers built from the ids a level uses. Masks and code name materials by id, never by layer index. formations = level geology class ids, habitats = habitat class ids this material suits. far_only materials are aerial tiles (30-90 m): sample them only in the far octave. Colour is as photographed elsewhere: the per-formation sets (terrain_sets) carry the Maine colour targets sampled from real material, which is how the colour rule is met. Legacy ids the editor already offers (rock, sand, cobble, forest, mud: the level's tex/*_diff.jpg) stay valid until World retires them.

materials._packed_doc: files.colour_height (RGB colour, A height) and files.normal_rough (RGB normal, A roughness), WebP, alpha exact: what the page reads (level.js, ledge.js, plants.js). colour/height/normal/rough stay for the tools. tools/assets/pack_materials.py

terrain_sets._doc: Proposed material set per bedrock formation and per habitat for levels/downeast (Assets proposes, World adopts: the level manifest's geology classes get a "set" pointing here, see docs/terrain-materials.md). Roles: face = steep rock (slope >= ~35 deg, triplanar), ledge = bare rock below that slope, rubble = loose stone at the foot of faces and on boulder/cobble habitat, lichen = overlay above the spray zone (w = its maximum weight), far = replaces the far octave beyond ~250 m. Two materials in a role blend by low-frequency noise with weights w, which breaks the tiling. colour_target: the sampled Maine colour the set is graded toward (shader multiplies by target / material mean, luminance-preserving); null = not sampled yet, draw as photographed. Habitat "wet" = the material below mean high water (the shader still darkens and glosses wet ground; this only swaps the texture).

formations.name: Bar Harbor Formation

colour_target.needs: Matt's photos of the Shore Path, Bar Harbor (dry and wet, overcast, a grey card or white paper in frame if possible); until then the materials draw as photographed

formations.note: Thin-bedded, jagged, layered. Both face materials carry straight beds along the texture u axis: project faces with rotation 0 so beds lie level (the formation dips gently; a per-class dip of ~10 deg would be the next refinement). marble_rock_03 on ledges breaks the bedding into the jagged blocks the Shore Path shows. gray_rocks (angular platy) is the talus. Ledge tops scale 1.0, faces 0.6 (thinner beds than the 2 m tiles).

formations.name: Cadillac Granite

colour_target.needs: Matt's photos of Otter Cliffs / Sand Beach headland / Thunder Hole ledge (dry, above the weed line, overcast); until then as photographed

formations.note: Coarse pink-grey, rounded, sheeted. tiger_rock (the coarse pink crystal grain) leads on the faces and dry_riverbed_rock (sub-horizontal sheet joints) is second: on tall cliff faces the jointed one repeated into a brick pattern, and the geometry now makes the sheets and joints itself (ledge brush, 18 Oct) (it is more saturated than Cadillac: the colour target will pull it down). Ledges: the coarse pink grain (tiger_rock) and the sheet joints (dry_riverbed_rock) both, so tops read as granite rather than marble; weathered grey comes from the lichen overlay (lichen_rock). marble_rock_01 was tried on the ledges and read as veined marble, so it is not in this set. Far octave: rocky_terrain (pink jointed slabs seen from 90 m) gives the ledge pattern from the water. Rubble: rounded granite cobbles.

colour_target.source: Nubble Lighthouse scan (Cape Neddick, Matt's upload nubble_lighthouse__cape_neddick_maine.glb): ortho of the scan, pixels on 25-70 deg slopes, not green, median of 612k px. Cape Neddick gabbro-diorite: right rock type, 100 km from MDI.

_cutoff_doc: cutoff_m (every model, 18 Oct house rule): the distance in metres beyond which the model is not drawn at all (World and lod.js honour it; the terrain texture, canopy texture or nothing takes over). Default = 300 x the model's size (its length; for poles and gangways the square root of its silhouette area, so a 6 m piling 0.3 m thick counts as 1.3 m), where it shrinks to about 3 px on a 1080-line screen with the sim's 50 deg camera, clamped to 60..5000 m; trees 1200 m (where their impostors already stop today; the canopy texture beyond). lod.js LOD.tiersFor caps every tier's far at cutoff_m, so it only ever shortens what draws. Tune per model in docs/perf.md.
models_pack_doc: models with "node": several share one file (a pack, for the page's file limit); MODELS fetches and parses the file once and takes each entry's node out of it
